page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-4 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the N1 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.3 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 26.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware. The CPU cache configuration consists of a 32 KB L1d cache, a 0.25 MB L2 cache, and a 45 MB L3 cache. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AES cryptography, BMI2, and FMA, while AVX-512 is unavailable.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the n1-highmem-4 delivers modest performance, generally placing in the lower tiers of modern cloud hardware. In CPU-intensive tests, the instance achieved a single-core stress-ng score of 1109.89 and a multi-core score of 2914.17, both categorized in the bottom 25%. Geekbench 5 testing yielded a single-core score of 924.0 and a multi-core score of 2032.0, placing in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show read speeds of 162.39 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 25.86 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write speed of 21.97 GB/sec. Redis SET operations reached 2.75 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput was measured at 2.82 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highmem-4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio on legacy hardware, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-performance compute capabilities. The tradeoff involves lower CPU performance and memory bandwidth compared to newer instance generations. This server is best suited for workloads such as moderate database caching, memory-constrained general-purpose applications, basic web serving, and lightweight background processing tasks that benefit from a larger memory footprint without demanding high CPU throughput.
